extracted.intended_audience: users/developers of the PARI/GP library doing number field computations (mathematicians, computational number theorists, and software developers)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP number-field (nf) library routines: descriptions of functions, expected inputs/outputs, flags, caveats, examples and recommended usage patterns for reliable number-field computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfcertify
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfcertify(GEN nf). Certify an nf structure so that nf.zk and nf.disc are correct; returns a vector of coprime composite integers if certification failed (these must be fully factored and their prime factors added to the prime table).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the returned vector is empty, then nf.zk and nf.disc are correct. Otherwise the result is dubious: completely factor each of the given integers, addprime each prime factor, then check nfdisc(nf.pol) equals nf.disc. Use nfcertify to turn a conditional nfinit([pol, listP]) into a certified nf; nfcertify may not run in polynomial time.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfcompositum
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfcompositum(GEN nf, GEN P, GEN Q, long flag). Given number field nf (base field K) and squarefree polynomials P,Q in K[X], outputs simple factors of the étale K-algebra A = K[X,Y]/(P(X),Q(Y)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns list of polynomials R (defining K[X]/(R)), sorted by increasing degree (lex order tie-breaker). Returns error if one polynomial not squarefree. More efficient to reduce to irreducible P and Q first (routine does not do this). There is a single factor R iff the number fields defined by P and Q are linearly disjoint. flag bits: bit 1 outputs vector of [R,a,b,k] where a (resp. b) expresses root of P (resp. Q) in K[X]/(R) and k small integer with b+ka = X mod R; bit 2 assumes P and Q irreducible and linearly disjoint and returns the single factor instead of a length-1 vector. Main variables of P and Q must be the same and have higher priority than nf (see varhigher/varlower). Example usage and recommendation: reduce complicated compositum polynomials using rnfpolredbest before further work.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfdetint
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfdetint(GEN nf, GEN x). Given a pseudo-matrix x, computes a non-zero ideal contained in (i.e. a multiple of) the determinant of x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful in conjunction with nfhnfmod to avoid coefficient explosion by supplying a determinant-multiple detx. Library syntax provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfdisc
rubrics_metrics.description: nfdisc(GEN T) — returns the discriminant of the number field Q[X]/(T) for integral, preferably monic, irreducible polynomial T using the Round 4 algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument T can be [T, listP] to return discriminant of an order whose basis is nfbasis(T,listP) (may not be maximal); valuations at primes in listP match field discriminant valuations. For p-adic discriminant use padicdisc(T,p) = p^valuation(nfdisc(T,[p]), p). See examples. Library syntax nfdisc(GEN T) (listP = NULL). Also see nfbasis which returns order basis and receives order discriminant via pointer.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfeltadd
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfeltadd(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN y). Given two elements x and y in nf, computes their sum x + y in the number field nf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple element addition in nf; example: nfeltadd(nf,1,x) returns 1+I for nf = nfinit(1+x^2).

rubrics_metrics.name: nfeltdiv
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfdiv(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN y). Given two elements x and y in nf, computes their quotient x/y in the number field nf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard division; complementary functions nfdivrem, nfdiveuc provide alternative quotient/rounding behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfeltdiveuc
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfdiveuc(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN y). Computes an algebraic integer q such that components of x - qy are reasonably small; functionally identical to round(nfdiv(nf,x,y)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when you want a nearest-integer quotient (Euclidean-like rounding) producing small remainder.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfeltdivmodpr (obsolete)
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfdivmodpr(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN y, GEN pr). Given x,y in nf and pr a prime ideal (modpr format), computes x/y modulo pr. This function is obsolete; use nfmodpr.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In library mode normally useless. Recommended workflow: project inputs to residue field (nf to Fq) then compute there; prefer nfmodpr and factormod variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfeltdivrem
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfdivrem(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN y). Given x,y in nf, returns [q,r] with x = qy + r where q is an algebraic integer and components of r are reasonably small.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives integral quotient and small remainder; useful when division with remainder in ZK is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfeltembed
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfeltembed(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN pl = NULL, long prec). Returns the real or complex embeddings of element x at current realprecision, controlled by optional pl argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: pl omitted: all r1+r2 embeddings. pl integer: return i-th embedding attached to i-th root of nf.pol. pl vector: vector of embeddings at specified real roots. Errors if index out of range. Use for numeric embeddings and evaluation; example provided for cubic field.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfeltmod
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfmod(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN y). Compute an element r = x - qy with q an algebraic integer and r small; functionally identical to x - nfmul(nf, round(nfdiv(nf,x,y)), y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for computing a canonical small remainder modulo y in nf.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfeltmul
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfmul(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN y). Computes product x * y in number field nf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard multiplication; use nfmulmodpr for modular variants (obsolete).

rubrics_metrics.name: nfeltmulmodpr (obsolete)
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfmulmodpr(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN y, GEN pr). Computes x*y modulo prime ideal pr (modpr format). Obsolete: use nfmodpr and work in residue field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In library mode normally useless; project inputs to residue field via nfmodprinit then compute.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfeltnorm
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfnorm(GEN nf, GEN x). Returns the absolute norm of element x in nf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard field norm calculation; use for arithmetic invariants.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfeltpow / nfinv / nfsqr
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfpow(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN k) computes x^k for integer k; nfinv and nfsqr correspond to k=-1 and k=2 respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use nfpow for general integer exponents; negative exponents compute inverses (requires invertibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: nfeltpowmodpr (obsolete)
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfpowmodpr(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN k, GEN pr). Computes x^k modulo prime ideal pr; obsolete — use nfmodpr and exponentiate in residue field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer working in residue field after nfmodprinit.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfeltreduce
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfreduce(GEN nf, GEN a, GEN id). Given ideal id in HNF and element a, finds r in nf such that a - r ∈ id and r is small.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computes canonical small representative modulo an ideal given in Hermite normal form.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfeltreducemodpr (obsolete)
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfreducemodpr(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN pr). Computes canonical representative for class of x modulo pr (prime ideal in modpr format). Obsolete: use nfmodpr.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project inputs to residue field via nfmodprinit and work in residue field instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfeltsign
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfeltsign(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN pl = NULL). Returns signs of real embeddings of x specified by optional pl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: pl omitted: vector of signs at all r1 real places. pl integer: sign at i-th real embedding. pl vector: signs at specified real roots. Errors if index > r1. Useful to check sign pattern across real places.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfelttrace
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nftrace(GEN nf, GEN x). Returns the absolute trace of x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard field trace; use for invariants and arithmetic checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfeltval / valuation helpers
rubrics_metrics.description: gpnfvalrem / nfvalrem / nfval and GEN gpnfvalrem(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN pr, GEN *y = NULL): compute valuation v at prime ideal pr of element x; optional &y returns y = x * τ^v where τ is an anti-uniformizer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The valuation of 0 is +oo. If y argument present, y is the part of x coprime to pr and integral when x is integral—useful to map to residue field more efficiently after making factors coprime to pr. nfvalrem returns LONG_MAX if x = 0 and valuation as long integer. idealval can be used when x is converted to a principal ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: nffactor
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nffactor(GEN nf, GEN T). Factorization of univariate polynomial T over number field nf; factors sorted by increasing degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Main variable of nf must be lower priority than T (Section 2.5.3). If nf was created conditionally via nfinit([T,listP]) then either run nfcertify or input nf.pol to avoid conditional issues: nffactor can recover in polynomial time when given pol but may miss factors if given conditional nf. Uses Belabas’s variant of van Hoeij’s algorithm and is polynomial-time in many cases; copes with hundreds of modular factors. Examples and caveats provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: nffactorback
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nffactorback(GEN nf, GEN f, GEN e = NULL). Reconstructs nf element corresponding to factorization f (with optional exponents e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interprets vector f (and e) as product of factors f[i]^e[i]; integer 1 corresponds to empty factorization. Accepts factorization matrix format. Useful to rebuild elements from factor lists; examples given.

rubrics_metrics.name: nffactormod (obsolete)
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nffactormod(GEN nf, GEN Q, GEN pr). Factor polynomial Q modulo prime ideal pr in nf; obsolete — use nfmodpr and factormod in residue field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coefficients of factors are lifted to elements of nf. Main variable constraints like nffactor apply. Using modprinit format is slightly faster due to precomputation. Prefer working in residue fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfgaloisapply
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN galoisapply(GEN nf, GEN aut, GEN x). Apply a Galois automorphism aut (given by image on field generator or as column vector) to an object x in the number field (element or ideal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: x can be element or ideal (not arbitrary vectors/matrices). Beware: applying automorphism to ideals may change representation so equality tests can fail even when ideals are equal; ideal equality can still be checked via idealval etc. Representing automorphism as column vector (algtobasis) is more efficient if used repeatedly. Performance example shows algtobasis form is faster.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfgaloisconj
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN galoisconj0(GEN nf, long flag, GEN d = NULL, long prec) or GEN galoisconj(GEN nf, GEN d). Computes conjugates (Q-automorphisms) of a root of polynomial defining nf; for non-Galois fields some conjugates may lie inside the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default (flag=0) uses combination of flags 4 and 1 and is complete. flag=1 uses nfroots (slow but polynomial-time). flag=4 uses galoisinit (very fast) but only applies to (most) Galois fields; may return only identity unless group is weakly super-solvable. d can be multiple of denominators of conjugates. Routine computes Q-automorphisms; K-automorphisms can be obtained via rnfgaloisconj trick shown in manual. Use galoisconj(GEN nf, GEN d) directly (flag 0).

rubrics_metrics.name: nfgrunwaldwang
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfgrunwaldwang(GEN nf, GEN Lpr, GEN Ld, GEN pl, long v = -1). Computes polynomial defining a cyclic extension of nf of minimal degree satisfying local degree conditions at specified primes and sign conditions at real places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input: Lpr vector of primes, Ld corresponding local degree multiples, pl vector for real places (pl[i] = -1 means complex). Degree is LCM of local degrees, search restricted to prime powers and construction to primes due to rnfkummer. If nf=Q accept primes as integers (primality not checked). Warning: if nf does not contain n-th roots of unity, computing bnf(nf(ζn)) may be triggered and be costly. Example given for quadratic base field.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfhilbert
rubrics_metrics.description: long nfhilbert0(GEN nf, GEN a, GEN b, GEN pr = NULL) / long nfhilbert(GEN bnf, GEN a, GEN b). Computes global quadratic Hilbert symbol (a,b) in nf; if pr provided compute local symbol modulo prime ideal pr.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Global symbol returns 1 if x^2 - a y^2 - b z^2 has a nontrivial solution in nf, -1 otherwise. Use local variant to test solvability modulo a given prime ideal from idealprimedec.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfhnf
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfhnf0(GEN nf, GEN x, long flag) / GEN nfhnf(GEN nf, GEN x). Given pseudo-matrix (A,I) returns pseudo-basis (B,J) in Hermite normal form of generated module; if flag non-zero also return transformation matrix U such that AU = [0|B].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The output pseudo-basis has integral, primitive ideals in J which are either trivial or non-principal. Use nfhnf to compute HNF of ZK-modules. Complementary function rnfsimplifybasis simplifies pseudo-basis by making ideals integral/primitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfhnfmod
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfhnfmod(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN detx). Given pseudo-matrix (A,I) and ideal detx (an integral multiple of determinant of (A,I)), finds pseudo-basis in HNF of module generated by (A,I) avoiding coefficient explosion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute detx via nfdetint to provide safe modulus; use to control size and speed of HNF computations. Helps efficiency in large computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfinit
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfinit0(GEN pol, long flag, long prec) and variants. Initialize number field nf attached to polynomial pol (preferably non-constant, monic, irreducible in Z[X]). nf is a structured row vector with components including nf.pol, nf.sign, nf.disc, nf.index, matrices M,G,roundG,T,M D,T I,M DI, nf.roots, nf.zk integral basis, power->integral basis matrix nf.zk->powers (nf[8]) and multiplication table (nf[9]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If non-monic polynomial is input, nfinit makes it monic then reduces via polredbest when flag=3 or flag=2. Accepts input nf/bnf/rnf in some cases. Special input [pol,B] accepted where B is integer basis or listP: compute order maximal at primes in listP and private prime table; result unconditional when discriminant factors completely over set. Use nfcertify to certify such conditional nf. Flags: nf_RED (find simpler defining polynomial), nf_ORIG (return change of variable), nf_ROUND2 (deprecated), nf_PARTIALFACT (deprecated lazy factorization). Examples, structure details, and huge discriminant caveats provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfinit with huge discriminant / special inputs
rubrics_metrics.description: nfinit accepts [pol, B] where B can be integer basis or listP specifying primes for which order is maximal; useful when discriminant is huge and factoring is hard; nfcertify can certify the result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag=2 produce polredbest reduced polynomial; flag=3 also return change of variable. Using nfinit([pol, 10^3]) computes an order maximal at primes ≤ 10^3; then use nfcertify to prove correctness (or find missing primes). If certification fails, an nf structure must be treated as untrusted. idealprimedec remains trustworthy for primes included in the initial list or primes not dividing any nfcertify output entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: isideal (nﬁsideal)
rubrics_metrics.description: long isideal(GEN nf, GEN x). Returns 1 if x is an ideal in number field nf, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether provided object is a valid ideal structure for nf.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfisincl
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfisincl(GEN f, GEN g). Given irreducible polynomials f and g (or nf structures) tests whether field defined by f is conjugate to a subfield of field defined by g. Returns 0 if not, else vector(s) of polynomials representing embeddings (a such that g | f∘a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If either input not irreducible result undefined. Using nf structures can be faster. Example timings show using nfinit for potential subfield accelerates repeated calls. Returns number of embeddings when used with # operator. Comparative performance notes and examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfisisom
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfisisom(GEN f, GEN g). Tests for isomorphism between fields defined by f and g (more efficient if f or g is nf structure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns number of isomorphisms (0 means not isomorphic). Usually very fast when answer is 'no' due to distinguishing invariants (degree, signature, discriminant). May be slower when fields share invariants; examples with timing given. Using nfinit structures speeds up repeated queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfislocalpower
rubrics_metrics.description: long nfislocalpower(GEN nf, GEN pr, GEN a, GEN n). Return 1 if a is an n-th power in the completed local field K_v for prime ideal pr, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show -1 being square but not a fourth power in certain ramified primes. Accepts vectors for a (to represent non-scalar elements) and large n; used to test local power conditions at primes above rational primes.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfkermodpr (obsolete)
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfkermodpr(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN pr). Kernel of matrix x in ZK/pr where pr is modpr format. Obsolete—prefer projecting to residue field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normally useless in library mode; project inputs to residue field (nf to FqM) and work there.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfmodpr
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfmodpr(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN pr). Map x to a t_FFELT in the residue field modulo pr. pr is either maximal ideal in idealprimedec format or modpr structure from nfmodprinit. nfmodprlift allows lifting back to ZK.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to number field elements (not recursive structures)—use apply to convert vectors/matrices/polynomials. Example shows mapping integral basis elements to residue field; use nfmodprinit to precompute modpr structure for speed.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfmodprinit
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfmodprinit(GEN nf, GEN pr). Transform prime ideal pr (from idealprimedec) into modpr format necessary for operations modulo pr in nf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use modpr format for repeated residue-field operations; saves time. Complementary functions nfmodpr and nfmodprlift handle projection and lifting.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfmodprlift
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfmodprlift(GEN nf, GEN x, GEN pr). Lift t_FFELT x from residue field modulo pr back to ring of integers; supports vectors, matrices, and polynomials via apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument pr may be maximal ideal or modpr structure. There is no compatibility check: behavior undefined if x is attached to different residue field than pr. Example shows how valuations reflect lift quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfnewprec
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfnewprec(GEN nf, long prec). Update nf structure to use current (usually larger) precision; works well if nf is bnf or bnr but may be slow as many principal ideal generators must be recomputed; bnf must contain fundamental units in latter case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also available: bnfnewprec and bnrnewprec. Use when higher precision is required; expect potentially expensive recomputations.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfpolsturm
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfpolsturm(GEN nf, GEN T, GEN pl = NULL). Given polynomial T with coefficients in nf, returns number of real roots of s(T) where s runs over real embeddings specified by pl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: pl omitted: all r1 real places. pl integer: i-th real embedding. pl vector: embeddings attached to listed real roots. Returns counts or vector of counts depending on pl. Errors if index exceeds number of real embeddings. Useful to count distinct real roots under embeddings.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfroots
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfroots(GEN nf = NULL, GEN x). Roots of polynomial x in number field nf (or in Q if nf omitted), without multiplicity. Coefficients of x may be scalar, polmod, polynomial, column vector. Main variable of nf must be lower priority than that of x unless coefs occur explicitly as polmods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: nfroots can accept a defining polynomial instead of nf (less efficient). Caveat: if nf was computed conditionally via nfinit([T,listP]) then either use nfcertify first or provide nf.pol to avoid missing factors: nfroots can recover in polynomial time in that case. See nfrootsQ for nf omitted case.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfrootsof1
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN rootsof1(GEN nf). Returns [w, z] where w is number of roots of unity in nf and z is a primitive w-th root of unity (in algebraic form).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm guesses w as gcd of #k(v)^* for unramified v above odd primes, then computes roots of corresponding cyclotomic polynomial in nf. Algorithm polynomial-time in field degree and bitsize of multiplication table; fields up to degree ~100 typically computed within a minute. Alternative algorithm rootsof1_kannan may be faster when roots of unity exist but can be exponential in worst case.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfsnf
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfsnf0(GEN nf, GEN x, long flag) / GEN nfsnf(GEN nf, GEN x). Given torsion ZK-module x (square integral invertible pseudo-matrix), returns Smith normal form ideal list D = [d1,...,dn] so x ≅ ZK/d1 ⊕ ... ⊕ ZK/dn with di | d{i-1}. If flag non-zero return [D,U,V] with U A V = identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input is integral pseudo-matrix [A,I,J] with integrality condition ai,j ∈ bi a^{-1} for all i,j; otherwise di may be non-integral. Every finitely generated torsion module is isomorphic to such a form. See Section 3.13.4.1 for integral pseudo-matrix definition and usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: nfsolvemodpr (obsolete)
rubrics_metrics.description: GEN nfsolvemodpr(GEN nf, GEN a, GEN b, GEN P). Solve a·x = b modulo prime ideal P (in modpr format) where a invertible over residue field and b column vector/matrix. Obsolete: use nfmodpr to project and solve in residue field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Function returns solution with coefficients lifted to nf elements. Preferred workflow: project to residue field using nfmodprinit and solve there, lifting results if needed.
